title: Blog Post 01
text:
Takeaway
A p-value is not “the probability that the null hypothesis is true.” It is “the probability of observing the current result, or a more extreme one, assuming that the null hypothesis is true.”
The key to understanding the p-value is not memorizing the number (0.05), but remembering the direction of the conditional probability:
\[
P(\text{Data}\mid H_0)
\neq
P(H_0\mid \text{Data})
\]
Once this distinction is clear, the p-value becomes much less mysterious.

title: About Me
text: I’m Guozhi Ye, a master’s student at the University of Pennsylvania studying Applied Economics and Data Science (AEDS). My academic interests focus on macroeconomic analysis, business analytics, and data-driven decision-making. I enjoy using economic reasoning and quantitative methods to better understand real-world business and economic problems. Alongside my graduate studies, I am developing practical technical skills in R, SQL, and Git to strengthen my ability to work with data, conduct reproducible analysis, and collaborate on analytical projects. Looking ahead, I hope to pursue a career that combines economics, data analysis, and business strategy.
